newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stock index ends down 2.73 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila stock index ends down 2.73 pct.

text.p: Manila stocks continued to fall sharply on Tuesday as foreign funds sold blue chips on fears property prices would crash as a result of a glut, traders said.
"There was more bloodbath today than yesterday. Nobody was spared," said Monique Lecaros, trader at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
The main index fell below its 2,950 support before plunging to a day's low of 2,887.37. It recovered slightly towards the close to end at 2,909.30, down 2.73 percent or 81.66 points.
The index has lost 9.73 percent since March 31 when it ended at 3,222.98.
Losers overwhelmed gainers 118 to 25, while prices of 49 issues remained unchanged, one broker said.

Traders said rumours that housing developer Empire East Land Holdings Inc and parent Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc were facing financial difficulties triggered fears of a property market crash. Both Megaworld and Empire East have denied financial troubles.
Foreign fund managers are also pulling out from the Philippine equities market due to a rise in U.S. bond rates.

Most property issues hit year-lows due to the sell down. Banks, which are still reeling from the effects of Victorias Milling Corp's cashflow crisis, were also bloodied on fears of a large exposure in the property sector.

"There's too much embedded froth in the real estate and banking issues, which unfortunately account for 50 percent of the composite index," said Joey Salceda, director of SBC Warburg, a unit of Swiss Banking Corp.

"The Philippine economy has been feasting on borrowed funds. Investors now realise this that we are likely to see a slowdown in foreign capital inflow partly due to rising interest rate in the United States," he added.
But other brokers said the foreign sell down was unjustified.
"It's an over reaction. They are comparing us with Thailand, but I don't think there's over building here at the moment," said Sun Hung Kai research director Raul Ruiz.
Traders said they expected a technical rebound when the market resumes on Thursday as some stocks are not at "very attractive levels." The market will remain closed on Wednesday due to a holiday.
